results.title: Roxadustat Does Not Affect Platelet Production, Activation, and Thrombosis Formation | Arteriosclerosis, Thrombosis, and Vascular Biology
results.content: For the in vitro experiments, platelets that had been isolated from healthy C57BL/6J mice and healthy volunteers were incubated with roxadustat or vehicle for 30 minutes, and platelet functional assays were performed to evaluate the effect of roxadustat on platelet function (Figure 1A). Mice that had received 5/6 nephrectomy (5/6 Nx) were orally administered roxadustat or vehicle or subcutaneously injected with EPO and multiple thrombosis models were performed to evaluate the effect of roxadustat on platelet activation and thrombosis formation in the state of chronic renal failure (Figure 4A). To assess the effect of roxadustat on platelet production in vivo, megakaryocytes in bone marrow sections from mice treated with the drug (20 mg/kg) or vehicle were subjected to immunohistochemistry. First, the aggregation of platelets pretreated with different concentration of roxadustat or vehicle was measured, and there was no remarkable effect on the aggregation induced by thrombin (0.033 U/mL), ADP (6 μM), U46619 (0.5 μg/mL), and collagen (2 μg/mL; Figure 1F and 1G). ### Roxadustat Administration Has No Effect on Platelet Activation and Thrombosis Formation in Healthy Mice In Vivo. To test whether roxadustat affects platelet function in vivo, healthy male mice were treated with roxadustat (20 mg/kg) or vehicle (DMSO, 1 μL/g) for 14 days—the time required for complete platelet turnover. To assess the effect of roxadustat on platelet production in vivo, we first compared the number of megakaryocytes (CD41[+]) in immunohistochemically stained bone marrow sections from mice treated with the drug (20 mg/kg) or vehicle (DMSO 1 μL/g body weight) for 14 days. ### Roxadustat Administration Has No Effect on Platelet Activation and Thrombosis Formation in 5/6 Nx Mice. To further evaluate the effect of roxadustat on platelet function in the pathological state of renal failure, roxadustat (20 mg/kg, thrice per week) or vehicle (DMSO, 1 µL/g body weight, thrice per week) was administrated for 2 weeks to mice that had underwent 5/6 Nx. Mice receiving EPO therapy (500 U/kg, thrice per week) were analyzed simultaneously as a positive control. Although roxadustat cannot activate platelets and cannot affect PT or APTT in healthy mice (Figure VA through VC in the Data Supplement), it may still be able to alter the risk of thrombosis in CKD patients through the coagulation or fibrinolytic systems.

Effect of pH levels on platelet aggregation and coagulation: a whole blood _in vitro_ study ### G Scharbert 1 Medical University Vienna, Austria Find articles by G Scharbert ### G Franta 1 Medical University Vienna, Austria Find articles by G Franta ### L Wetzel 1 Medical University Vienna, Austria Find articles by L Wetzel ### S Kozek-Langenecker 2 Evangelical Hospital, Vienna, Austria Find articles by S Kozek-Langenecker 1 Medical University Vienna, Austria 2 Evangelical Hospital, Vienna, Austria ### Supplement _31st International Symposium on Intensive Care and Emergency Medicine_ ### Conference 31st International Symposium on Intensive Care and Emergency Medicine This is an Open Access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (), which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original work is properly cited. Whether acidosis leads to a reduced platelet function has not so far been evaluated. In this _in vitro_ study we evaluated the effects of pH levels (7.6, 7.4, 7.2, 7.0 and 6.8) on platelet aggregation and coagulation with human whole blood of healthy male volunteers. We used multiple electrode aggregometry (MEA) Multiplate® (tests: ADP, ASPI, TRAP) for platelet function testing. The global coagulation was evaluated at pH 6.8 and 7.4 with ROTEM®, which is a rotational thrombelastometry (tests: NATEM and APTEM). The pH levels of the blood samples were achieved by titration of HCl and NaOH. In MEA the AUC was significantly reduced for pH 7.0 and pH 6.8 in all three tests (ADP, ASPI and TRAP), as well as aggregation and velocity. Platelet function was not influenced by alkalosis (pH 7.6). The α-angle and lysis index for 60 minutes were significantly reduced at pH 6.8. In our study we evaluated a significant decrease of platelet function at pH 7.0 and 6.8 with MEA. The results of the analysis with the ROTEM® system showed a significant reduction of thrombus formation at pH 6.8, as described in the literature.

results.title: Coagulation Tests - DynaMed
results.content: # Coagulation Tests. * Coagulation tests are a vital part of the investigation for defects in hemostasis, as well as for monitoring treatment used in the prevention and/or management of thrombotic and bleeding disorders.2. * PubMed31069971International journal of laboratory hematologyInt J Lab Hematol2019050141 Suppl 1162-169162Coagulation tests qualitatively or quantitatively measure the presence or activity of target component(s) (analyte[s]) (Int J Lab Hematol 2019 May;41 Suppl 1:162). * Routine coagulation screening tests include prothrombin time (PT)/INR, activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT), Clauss fibrinogen assay, thrombin time (TT), and D-dimer assay.3. * Some common indications for obtaining routine coagulation tests may include:3. + Patients with clinical manifestations suggestive of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). * Coagulation tests as part of the investigation of hemostasis abnormalities:. + After a thorough evaluation of patient history and physical and evaluation of medication intake, if a patient is suspected of having an abnormality in hemostasis, routine coagulation tests are often performed as part of initial laboratory investigation along with other baseline tests, which may include:. + Follow-up evaluation will vary depending on the initial testing results. Follow-up tests may include, but are not limited to:1. - Platelet function testing (for example, light transmission aggregometry) in patients with normal routine coagulation screening. - Mixing studies to detect the presence of inhibitors against coagulation factors, as well as the presence of lupus anticoagulant in patients with prolonged PT and/or aPTT. - Tests to evaluate individual coagulation factor activities. + See Diagnostic Testing in Easy Bruising - Approach to the Patient and Bleeding Disorders - Approach to the Patient for additional information. * In addition, viscoelastic studies, which evaluate global hemostasis, are used to monitor abnormalities in hemostasis and help guide management (for example, administration of blood products) in patients with major bleeding (Am J Hematol 2014 Feb;89(2):228).
